questions.knowledge_point: Identifying True Statements Regarding Left- and Right-Continuity
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14008055/assets/718dd1f38f7c790ab83639f69462b372de6b7e8501c0a4d6ff678340ab4154bd.png)

Which of the following statements are true regarding the function $y=f(x)$ plotted above?

- The function is left-continuous at $x=0$
- The function is right-continuous at $x=0$
- The function is continuous at $x=0$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's look at each statement in turn:

- Statement I is false.  The function is not left-continuous at $x=0,$ since the left-sided limit is not equal to the function value:

$$
{lim}_{x\to {0}^{-}}f(x)=3\ne 0=f(0)
$$

- Statement II is true. The function is right-continuous at $x=0,$ since the right-sided limit is equal to the function value:

$$
{lim}_{x\to {0}^{+}}f(x)=0=f(0)
$$

- Statement III is false. In order for the function to be continuous at $x=0,$ it must be both left-continuous and right-continuous. However, we have already determined that the function is not left-continuous at this point.

In conclusion, only statement II is true.

questions.knowledge_point: Using the Definition of Left- and Right-Continuity to Compute a Limit
questions.problem: If $f(x)$ is right-continuous at $x=-5$ and ${lim}_{x\to (-5)^{+}}f(x)=3,$ then what is ${lim}_{x\to (-5)^{+}}(f(x)-2f(-5))?$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $f(x)$ is right-continuous at $x=-5,$ we must have

$$
{lim}_{x\to (-5)^{+}}f(x)=f(-5)=3.
$$

Consequently,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (-5)^{+}}(f(x)-2f(-5)) & ={lim}_{x\to (-5)^{+}}f(x)-2f(-5) \\  & =3-2\cdot 3 \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
If $f(x)$ is left-continuous at $x=-1$ and ${lim}_{x\to (-1)^{-}}f(x)=-6,$ then what is 
${lim}_{x\to (-1)^{-}}(2f(x)-xf(-1))?$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $f(x)$ is left-continuous at $x=-1,$ we must have

$$
{lim}_{x\to (-1)^{-}}f(x)=f(-1)=-6.
$$

Consequently,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (-1)^{-}}(2f(x)-xf(-1)) & =2{lim}_{x\to (-1)^{-}}f(x)-f(-1){lim}_{x\to (-1)^{-}}x \\  & =2(-6)-(-6)(-1) \\  & =-18.\end{aligned}
$$
